title: Acid strength and molecular structure (AP)
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AB10#t3 term and clue written for the game; AB10#t1 term and clue written for the game; AB10#t4 term and clue written for the game; AB10#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AB10#N.4, AB10#N.8, AB10#N.10, AB10#N.11.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Carboxylic acid
items.clue: A compound of the class R–COOH, in which only one hydrogen is donated.

items.label: Inductive effect
items.clue: Atoms such as Cl pull electron density toward themselves through σ bonds.

items.label: Conjugate base
items.clue: The A⁻ left when HA donates H⁺; the more stable it is, the stronger HA is.

items.label: Resonance
items.clue: Spreads a negative charge over several atoms, as over both O atoms in CH₃COO⁻.

questions.stem: Hypochlorous acid, HClO, and hypoiodous acid, HIO, are both weak acids. Which choice identifies the stronger of the two acids and gives a correct reason?

options.text: HClO, because the H–Cl bond in HClO is more polar than the H–I bond in the molecule HIO
HIO, because acid strength increases down group 17, just as it does from HCl to HBr to HI
HClO, because Cl is more electronegative than I and stabilizes the conjugate base more
HIO, because the less electronegative I atom holds the electrons, and so the H atom, less tightly

questions.stem: Ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH, and ethanol, CH₃CH₂OH, both contain an O–H group. Ethanoic acid is a weak acid; ethanol does not measurably ionize in water. Which statement best explains the difference?

options.text: Ethanoic acid has more H atoms bonded to oxygen, so it has more protons to donate.
The O–H bond in ethanol is more polar, so its H atom is held more tightly.
Ethanol is a stronger base than water, so it takes H⁺ back as soon as it is lost.
In ethanoate the negative charge is shared over two O atoms by resonance.

questions.explanation: Delocalization stabilizes CH₃COO⁻. In CH₃CH₂O⁻ the charge sits on one O atom, so that ion forms far less readily.

questions.stem: HBr is a strong acid. A student dissolves KBr(s) in pure water at 25°C to make a 0.10 M solution; the K⁺ ion does not react with water. Which prediction of the pH of the solution, with its reason, is correct?

options.text: Close to 13, because the conjugate base of a strong acid is itself a strong base
Equal to 7, because Br⁻ is too weak a base to remove H⁺ ions from water molecules
Slightly above 7, because an ion with a negative charge pulls H⁺ ions out of water
Slightly below 7, because Br⁻ comes from the acid HBr and keeps some of its acidity

questions.explanation: Br⁻ is so stable that it has a negligible tendency to accept a proton. Neither ion reacts with water, so the pH is 7 at 25°C.

questions.stem: Four acids are each made up as 0.10 M solutions at 25°C: CH₃COOH, CH₃CH₂COOH, FCH₂COOH and BrCH₂COOH. Which solution has the lowest pH, and why?

options.text: CH₃CH₂COOH, because its longer carbon chain supplies more electron density to the –COOH group.
BrCH₂COOH, because Br is the largest of these atoms and so takes the negative charge itself.
FCH₂COOH, because F is the most electronegative and best stabilizes the conjugate base.
CH₃COOH, because without a halogen nothing holds back its acidic hydrogen atom.

questions.explanation: F pulls electron density away from –COO⁻ most strongly, spreading its charge. pKa: FCH₂COOH 2.59, the strongest acid here, so the lowest pH.
